output.myth: When the Gale Tavo took a boat off the skerries, the men went down under the grey water and did not come up. Their wives set the kettle on and waited. In the morning the shags stood on the black rock with their wings held out to dry, and the old women said that was the drowned, come up to spread their cloth in the wind before they flew north. Mother Hesk told the wives not to look too long. A shag that is watched keeps its wings spread and never leaves the rock. Sil, who searches the dark for her brother Aun, has seen them too, and she says they are only drying their sails. Kael the Netter comes down at low tide with his empty net to fish for lamps. He has never caught one. So when you see the birds on the skerry at dawn, turn from them, put the kettle on, say the names of the ones who did not come home, then go in and mend your nets.
output.verse:
Wings spread on the rock,
the drowned dry their sails at dawn,
turn from them. Go mend.
